findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without washing their hands. Education was conducted with the PIC as there was a language barrier in effect with staff. They were instructed to pass along the instructions to staff and ensure that effective hand washing was taking place at all times that it is required in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was observed with a large trash can in front of it, blocking access. The PIC saw this as the inspector walked up to it and moved the trash can to correct and allow access. The situation was discussed and they are aware that the hand sink must remain accessible at all times in the facility to promote good hand washing practices in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival two knives were observed stored in the gap between the prep coolers. This gap was visibly soiled and could not be considered a clean or safe surface for food contact items. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Two seperate wiping cloths were observed on the counters throughout the facility. Education was conducted and the PIC moved the cloths to the sani bucket to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all rags used on food contact surfaces are stored between use in a sanitizer solution of sufficient concentration to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shell eggs and raw pork stored on top of buckets containing ready-to-eat (RTE) sauces in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was an informed and the items were rearranged. Ensure raw animal foods are stored below RTE foods to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed four dented cans in the dry storage shelf of the kitchen space. The PIC was informed and the cans were removed from use. In the future, set aside any dented cans and return to distributor. Dented and damaged cans can cause bacterial growth which leads to botulism contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket in prep line to measure 0ppm chlorine. PIC was informed of the low sanitizer concentration, and a new bucket was made. PIC stated that the bucket was made this morning. The chlorine in the bucket may have evaporated in that time, causing the low concentration. Ensure staff are checking the sanitizer concentration frequently and replacing when necessary.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed bare wood on shelving and next to fryers in kitchen. Bare wood next to the fryers is being used to cover the gap between the fryer and the counter. The bare wood on the shelving is above the microwave and used to extend shelves. Bare wood can harbor bacteria due to its absorbent characteristics. Ensure the shelving is painted or covered to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed kitchen hand sink to be blocked by garbage can. Garbage can was moved during inspection.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed bucket of sanitizer solution to test at 50 ppm Cl-. New sanitizer solution was made during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed single service plastic forks to be stored with the food contact surface facing up. Store single service utensils in a manner that protects against contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed 2 unfinished wooden boards used under fryer. Seal or remove wood from underneath fryers. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.
